title: Font styles for dyslexic readers in screen-reading experiment
statement:
For dyslexic readers in a screen-reading experiment, sans-serif, monospaced, and roman styles outperformed serif, proportional, and italic styles, supporting a font menu built from accessible options such as Arial, Helvetica, Verdana, and Courier rather than assuming one universal typeface.

Options:
- Accessible sans: Arial (fits: professional, accessible)
- Neutral sans: Helvetica (fits: minimal, professional)
- Open sans: Verdana (fits: friendly, screen first)
- Monospaced: Courier (fits: technical, utilitarian)
- Roman option: Computer Modern Unicode (fits: academic, editorial)
appliesWhen: Applies to: accessibility, content sites, education, web apps. Audience: adults, general.

source.title: Good fonts for dyslexia
source.venue: Proceedings of the 15th International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility
